purpose: Prove the openai-api provider path supports the FULL Route D child command (isolation argv + -C + --output-schema + stdin sentinel) and that its event stream classifies clean, BEFORE consuming Route D's one-shot research attempt.
command_fidelity: codex_command() taken VERBATIM from research_loop.py. The ONLY substitution was the -C value (run dir -> scratch dir) so nothing was written into the sealed surface. --output-schema still pointed at the real ROUTE_D/OUTPUT_SCHEMA.json.
env_fidelity: Exactly the minimal dict native_reason() builds: HOME, PATH, LANG, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, TMPDIR, OPENAI_API_KEY. This also proved the mise codex shim resolves under that restricted PATH.
prompt_sent: Reply with exactly this object and nothing else: {"action":{"kind":"final","report":"ok"}}
prompt_content_note: Mechanically neutral. Carries NO benchmark or research content, same class as the four probes enumerated in W01_RUNNER_AVAILABILITY.json.

attempt_accounting.reason: Nothing in this probe touches RESUME_AUTHORIZATION.json, loop_state/ or the Ledger. It is a runner-capability probe, not a route dispatch.

RESULTS.normalize_output: PASS -- returned {kind: final, report: ok}, i.e. the OUTPUT_SCHEMA round-tripped through the Responses API strict json_schema surface AND through validate_action().

usage_findings: Codex instruction preamble + output schema costs ~10,880 input tokens before any payload. The earlier 8,235-token figure was measured WITHOUT --output-schema.

cache_write_input_tokens=10899 proves automatic prompt caching is ACTIVE on this provider path. That matters: Route D's ~319 KB payload sorts acceptance_schema first, so the expensive prefix should cache across the loop's turns.
reasoning_output_tokens=0 at model_reasoning_effort=high for a trivial prompt -- effort is not a floor.

stderr_finding.observed: ONE line: 'ERROR codex_models_manager::manager: failed to refresh available models: ... missing field `models`', followed by the raw /v1/models JSON body (~21.9 KB).
stderr_finding.explanation: Codex's model-catalogue refresher expects the ChatGPT-backend response shape (a `models` field). The standard OpenAI /v1/models returns {object:list, data:[...]}. Codex logs the decode failure and proceeds; the turn completed with returncode 0.
stderr_finding.material_finding: gpt-6-astra IS present in the account's /v1/models listing, so the pinned benchmark subject is genuinely available on the API-metered path.
stderr_finding.cost_note: This dump lands in every run/turn_NN_native.json via screen(). ~21.9 KB of noise per turn. It contains no secret material and passed screen() cleanly.

served_model_attestation.detail: The codex exec --json event stream carries NO model identifier -- thread.started, turn.started, item.completed and turn.completed contain none. research_loop.py already records served_model='UNKNOWN' for this reason; that is honest, not a defect introduced by the amendment. What IS established: the request pins -c model="gpt-6-astra", and that id exists on the account, so the API did not silently substitute an unknown-model fallback (it would have returned an error instead).
